entities.title: No clocks
entities.summary: Online games have no time control.
entities.impact: A player who stops answering holds the game in play for ever; nothing ends it but resigning, a draw or mate.
entities.details: The reason abandoned exists in the types, but nothing sets it.

entities.title: No notice of a move
entities.summary: Only new invitations are emailed; a move reaches the other player only while the game or the lobby is open.
entities.impact: A player learns of a move by opening Friends: the lobby and the tab's title show what waits.

entities.title: Only the two players see a game
entities.summary: There are no spectators: a game, its transcript and its live connection are for its players only.
entities.impact: A friend cannot watch a game, even finished.

entities.title: No phone-sized layout
entities.summary: The game screen needs about 1000 px of width.
entities.impact: On a phone the game panel and the board crowd each other.

entities.title: The computer plays only in the browser
entities.summary: Stockfish runs in the page; the desktop build has no computer opponent.
entities.impact: Playing the computer from the editor or a desktop build says it needs the web version.

entities.title: Invitations do not expire
entities.summary: An open invitation stays open until it is answered or cancelled.
entities.impact: Old invitations wait in both lobbies until someone answers them.

entities.title: 30 invitations an hour
entities.summary: A player can send at most 30 invitations in any hour.
entities.impact: The 31st is refused with "That's a lot of challenges. Try again in an hour."

entities.title: Lists are capped
entities.summary: The lobby lists 50 invitations each way and 50 games in play, 500 contacts, 200 games with one contact; history comes 30 at a time.
entities.impact: A player with more sees only the newest.

entities.title: One game against the computer per device
entities.summary: The device keeps one game against the computer; starting another replaces it.
entities.impact: A game in play against the computer is lost when a new one starts.
